questions.q: What is the main point of the article?
options: Male bonobos are more aggressive hunters than male chimpanzees
Female bonobos lead most hunts, challenging the 'man the hunter' story
Chimpanzees were found to hunt less than bonobos in Congo
Bonobo hunting is dying out as Congo's rainforest shrinks
questions.explain: New research shows female bonobos are the primary hunters, which challenges the man-the-hunter origin story.

questions.q: Who typically led the majority of hunts recorded in the study?
options: Older, more dominant females
Young solitary males
Males and females equally
Only immature bonobos
questions.explain: The data showed it was typically the older, more dominant females who led most hunts.

questions.q: What was the most common prey of the bonobos?
options: Red colobus monkey
Wild forest pig
Pygmy flying squirrel
Grey parrot nestling
questions.explain: The most common prey was the red colobus monkey, which required coordinated teamwork.

questions.q: According to Dr. Fruth, what do dominant female bonobos do with hunted meat?
options: Keep it all for their own young
Hand it to the males to reward them
Share it to form alliances
Bury it for the dry season
questions.explain: Dominant females dole out meat as a way to form alliances.

questions.q: What does the article imply about the link between hunting and physical strength?
options: Physical strength is the main factor in hunting success
Male bonobos hunt less because they are weaker
Hunting ability is not necessarily about big muscles
Females hunt only when the males are absent
questions.explain: Males are larger and stronger but not dominant, showing hunting is not necessarily about big muscles.
